basic_info.name: Superpower (Superpower Health, Inc., superpower.com)
basic_info.category: Consumer preventive-health membership platform — blood lab testing + tracking app + AI concierge/care team + supplements/prescriptions marketplace ('world's first health super app', longevity/preventive-care positioning)
basic_info.country: United States (HQ Los Angeles, CA; nationwide US cash-pay service; surcharge/pricing variance in New York and New Jersey due to state lab laws)
basic_info.stage: Growth-stage startup: founded 2023 by Jacob Peters, Max Marchione and Kevin Unkrich; national launch April 22, 2025 with $30M Series A; still private, no Series B announced as of Aug 2026
basic_info.pricing_model: CONFIRMED multi-source (was single-source doubt): launched Apr 2025 at $499/yr (2 blood draws/yr), then cut price by 60% to $199/yr on Aug 19, 2025 (Endpoints exclusive; own homepage; Yahoo Finance PR). Current model: $199/yr billed annually, includes 100+ biomarker panel once at the start of each year, no hidden fees, HSA/FSA eligible, cancel anytime. NY/NJ members pay ~$399 [uncertain]. At-home phlebotomist draw +$99 when no Quest nearby. Add-ons on top: Advanced Panel $189, Gut Microbiome $239, Toxins Panel $299, Grail Galleri multi-cancer screen, DunedinPACE Pace of Aging, Health Score test. Employer/organization plans offered.
basic_info.target_user: US health-optimization consumers (~28-55: biohackers, athletes, professionals), framed also for the chronic-condition mass market (PR cites 194M US adults with chronic conditions); employers/organizations as B2B2C channel
basic_info.scale_metrics: 64,000+ members (own homepage claim, Aug 2026) vs ~150k launch waitlist reported in 2025 — fast but self-reported; total funding $51M over 2 rounds ($30M Series A, Apr 22 2025, led by Forerunner Ventures with Susa, Long Journey, Day One, Bond Capital, Winklevoss Capital and celebrity angels incl. Giannis Antetokounmpo, Logan Paul, Vanessa Hudgens, Steve Aoki, Balaji Srinivasan); post-Series A valuation reported >$300M [uncertain — other trackers cite ~$150M]; estimated revenue ~$10.5M [uncertain, ZoomInfo]; Forbes 30 Under 30 Healthcare 2026 list. Durable-threat read: the member growth (0 to 64k in ~16 months) plus a celebrity/influencer demand engine and the $199 anchor price make it a credible mass-market winner; noise factors: waitlist numbers, self-reported member count, and unverified revenue/valuation.

product.core_features: Annual 100+ biomarker blood panel from a single draw (hormones, thyroid, heart, metabolic, inflammation, nutrients, liver, kidney, etc., ~10-21 categories); results dashboard with optimal/functional ranges; overall Health Score; Biological Age and Pace of Aging (DunedinPACE); 24/7 AI health concierge chat with full personal data context; 24/7 human care team messaging; personalized evidence-based protocol (diet, lifestyle, supplements); upload of past/external lab reports with AI-powered trend analysis; wearable sync (Apple Health, Whoop, Oura, etc.); marketplace for supplements (member discounts), prescriptions and peptides; add-on panels (Advanced $189, Gut $239, Toxins $299, Galleri MCED); employer/organization plans
product.signature_differentiator: The aggressive democratization play: a full 'test + track + coach' bundle at a $199/yr 'less-than-Netflix' anchor (60% price cut Aug 2025), executed through single-draw 100+ biomarker logistics at 2,000+ Quest sites or at-home phlebotomy, wrapped in an AI concierge + 24/7 care team and an action-loop marketplace (supplements/prescriptions/peptides/add-on tests incl. cancer screening). No US competitor bundles all of this at that price point — Function Health charges $365-499 for 160 biomarkers 2x/yr without AI coaching.
product.lab_data_handling: Own membership orders the labs; one blood draw covers 100+ biomarkers; cadence is 1x/year at base $199 (the original $499 tier included 2 draws/yr — the 2025 cut halved frequency to hit the price point); collection at 2,000+ Quest Diagnostics locations (10-min draw) or at-home phlebotomist for +$99 in major metros; results in ~10 days or less; physician-led interpretation through the care team; retesting and depth via paid add-ons (Advanced Panel, gut microbiome, toxins, Galleri MCED, Pace of Aging). No CGM or own hardware; wearable data is synced, not produced.
product.family_dependents_depth: None found: no family plan, dependent profiles, caregiver mode, pediatric reference ranges or hereditary-risk features are marketed anywhere on the site or press — a parent is just a separate paid account (one Trustpilot member 'signed up my parents as well', i.e., 3 separate memberships). This is a wide-open pillar for Dr. Exame (family/dependents depth is explicitly absent in the US leader too).
product.doctor_sharing: Weak/absent: care happens inside their own 24/7 text care team + AI concierge (physician replies within ~12-24h); the 1:1 clinician consult that existed in the base package was removed around Sept 2025 (company confirmed on Trustpilot after a false-advertising complaint, refunded the member). No consultation brief, SOAP export or 'share with your own doctor' feature is published; a Sept 2025 user reported labs could not even be downloaded as PDF from the website [uncertain current state]. Positioning is replacing/sidestepping the PCP, not equipping him.
product.action_loop_monetization: Textbook action-loop economics after the interpretation: personalized protocol pushes members to the in-app marketplace — supplements with member discounts, prescription access and peptides via affiliated telehealth providers — plus a ladder of add-on tests (Advanced Panel $189, Gut $239, Toxins $299, Grail Galleri MCED, biological-age panels) and the annual renewal/retest cycle. The $199 membership is the acquisition wedge; margin lives in add-ons, marketplace attach and renewals (mirroring the industry shift where the money migrated from the report to the action loop).

technology.ai_approach: In-house AI health concierge ('24/7 AI health advisor', 'advanced AI chat') grounded on the member's full context — labs, wearables, intake questionnaire; generates evidence-backed protocols (diet/lifestyle/supplements) and answers biomarker questions instantly. Hybrid human-in-the-loop: care team physicians handle escalation via text (~24h SLA) and oversee the medical layer. No published model details, accuracy metrics or methodology [uncertain].
technology.data_inputs: Membership blood panel (100+ biomarkers); uploaded external/past bloodwork reports (any lab) feeding AI trend detection; wearables via Apple Health, Whoop, Oura and similar; deep onboarding health-history questionnaire; optional gut microbiome, toxins and Galleri add-ons.
technology.data_interoperability: IN is strong for a consumer product: Quest lab ordering/results pipeline, external lab report upload (PDF) with AI parsing across any historical lab, wearable sync. OUT is weak: no FHIR, no public API, no Apple Health Records / Health Connect medical-records integration, and no PDF export surfaced (a Sept 2025 user reported downloads were not possible from the web) [uncertain current state]. No WhatsApp-class channel (US product). Broad ingestion + closed egress = data-roach-motel pattern.
technology.platform: Web-first (launched web-only, app came later); iOS app now on the App Store; Android availability unconfirmed [uncertain]. No public developer API.

ux.onboarding: Sign-up → deep health-history + goals questionnaire → schedule blood draw (Quest walk-in or at-home phlebotomist) → results within ~10 days → dashboard, Health Score, biological age and personalized protocol. Time-to-value roughly 1-2 weeks (mostly lab turnaround), praised as streamlined in reviews.
ux.data_visualization: Clean dashboard praised in reviews: 100+ biomarkers with optimal/functional ranges and plain-language explanations, a single overall Health Score as north star, Biological Age + Pace of Aging benchmarking, and AI trend detection across uploaded historical labs regardless of originating lab.
ux.engagement_channel: Retention rides the annual test-and-protocol cycle: 24/7 AI chat + SMS/text care team, blood-draw reminders with the order attached, protocol that 'evolves with you', supplement repurchases with member discounts, and add-on test upsells. No community, streaks or WhatsApp-style channel found — engagement is app/SMS-centric, which in a BR context would be a structural retention gap.

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: No published accuracy claims, peer-reviewed validation or methodology for the interpretation layer; credibility built via physician leadership (Chief Longevity Officer Anant Vinjamoori, Harvard MD/MBA; advisors incl. Dr. Leigh Erin Connealy and UCLA's Dr. Robert Lufkin; press releases cite a Harvard/Stanford/Oxford medical advisory board) and CLIA-certified lab execution through Quest. Trustpilot 4.6/5 but on a tiny base of 48 reviews. Documented trust incidents (2025): 1:1 clinician consult silently removed from the base package while the AI bot still advertised it (company refunded after false-advertising complaint); no web PDF lab export; SMS-only support with 12-24h latency; zip-code-only lab finder pushing users to the $99 at-home fee. Billing transparency is otherwise marketed as a feature (flat price, no hidden fees, HSA/FSA).
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: US cash-pay wellness + telehealth hybrid: labs run through CLIA-certified Quest, membership marketed as preventive/wellness with HSA/FSA eligibility, prescriptions and peptides routed via affiliated medical providers, aggressive 'detect early signs of 1,000+ conditions' marketing claims without FDA SaMD clearance or published device-grade validation. NY/NJ pricing variance reflects state lab-law friction. No LGPD/ANVISA exposure (US-only, English-only). For the Dr. Exame benchmark: Superpower shows how far the wellness line can be pushed in the US (condition-detection claims, peptide sales) under a physician-led brand — a posture that would not survive ANVISA RDC 657/2022 SaMD scrutiny in Brazil, where Dr. Exame's explicit non-diagnostic guardrails are a compliance asset, not a weakness.
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they DON'T do (Dr. Exame openings): no family/dependents/caregiver mode or pediatric ranges; no hereditary-risk layer; no doctor-facing consultation brief/SOAP or clean record export (they compete with the PCP instead of arming him); base cadence cut to 1x/year (2x costs more or needs add-ons); no WhatsApp-class engagement; no non-US/non-English market; no transparent accuracy methodology; singles only. What WORKS (inspiration, not copy): the $199 'less-than-Netflix' anchor reframing premium testing as a mass-market subscription; single-draw 100+ biomarker logistics via 2,000+ Quest sites + at-home option; AI concierge + human care team hybrid at 24/7; Health Score + Biological Age/Pace of Aging as legible north-star metrics; upload any historical lab → AI trend analysis as ingestion wedge; add-on ladder (gut, toxins, Galleri MCED) that grows ARPU without touching the anchor price; celebrity/investor-driven demand engine (Giannis, Logan Paul) and waitlist marketing.
trust_gaps.relevance: High — Superpower is the closest existing proof of the 'testing + tracking + coach' bundled membership at a mass price, and the $199 price cut (Aug 2025, now multi-source confirmed) is the single most important pricing signal in the consumer lab category. Direct benchmark for Dr. Exame's premium tier strategy; its structural gaps (family, doctor loop, export/interoperability, annual-only cadence, no BR presence) map almost exactly onto Dr. Exame's differentiation pillars.
